'''Adolf Goetzberger''' (29 November 1928 – 24 February 2023) was a German physicist.

== Life and career ==
Goetzberger studied physics in [[Munich]], Germany. He finished his university studies with a work over ''Über die Kristallisation aufgedampfter Antimonschichten''. He worked together with [[William Shockley]] in [[Palo Alto, California|Palo Alto]], California and for company [[Bell Labs]].  In 1981, Goetzberger founded [[Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems ISE]] in [[Freiburg im Breisgau]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.epo.org/learning-events/european-inventor/finalists/2009/goetzberger.html|title=The Sun God|first=European Patent|last=Office|website=www.epo.org}}</ref>

Goetzberger died on 24 February 2023, at the age of 94.<ref>{{cite news |title=Deutscher Solarpionier Adolf Goetzberger gestorben |url=https://science.apa.at/power-search/16526166364345438526 |access-date=1 March 2023 |publisher=APA |date=1 March 2023}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* [[J J Ebers Award]]
* [[European Inventor Award]]
* Doctor honoris by [[University of Freiburg]], 1971
* Honorary doctorate from the Faculty of Science and Technology at [[Uppsala University]], [[Sweden]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/honorary-doctorates/|title=Honorary doctorates – Uppsala University, Sweden|first=David|last=Naylor|website=www.uu.se|date=9 June 2023 }}</ref> 1995
* Karl Boer medal, 1997
* [[Becquerel Prize]], 1997
* [[Photovoltaic Specialists Conference|William R. Cherry Award]], 1997
* Einstein Award, 2006
* European Solar Award, 2009 
* Officer's Cross of the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]]
* [[Order of Merit of Baden-Württemberg]]
